1	# Agent Note: The read barrier as filesystem and process authority
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-05-read-barrier.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	A certificate proves only what the implementer could not reach, and nothing in the repository decides that. [`dsh-verification`](../../../../packages/verification/verification/README.md) commits a `verification/certificate` only for a fully passing run and stamps it with a `CertificateIsolation` of `none`, `process`, or `host`, but its own Known Limitations name the missing read barrier: the standard's `run` instructions are readable by any in-process consumer of the log, and denying implementer reads is filesystem-policy work in a plugin that does not exist. The [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) states the requirement as principle P4, the read barrier as filesystem and process authority rather than a promise; this note is its design.
10	
11	The implementer and the checks share one filesystem and one operating-system user. `EnvironmentRunner.run()` creates the implementer's agent with `meta.cwd = workspace` and then executes every check through `ctx.shell` with `workdir: workspace` from the same process ([`packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts`](../../../../packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts)); its README states that the read barrier is the deployment's. The standard is in the implementer's own session log, which [`dsh-session-persistence-jsonl`](../../../../packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/README.md) keeps as ordinary files under its configured root. [`dsh-credentials-local`](../../../../packages/credentials/credentials-local/README.md) already records what that costs: owner-only modes stop other operating-system users and not the model, because tool processes run as the same user and the shipped file policy confines mutations rather than reads.
12	
13	Composition decides what an implementer can read, and no composition is checked. A preset that mounts [`dsh-tool-session-query`](../../../../packages/session-query/tool-session-query/README.md) hands the model five tools that read the durable session log; one that mounts [`dsh-tool-cordis`](../../../../packages/extensions/tool-cordis/README.md) lets it define and mount a plugin into the live process. `tools.restrict()` and subagent `toolFilter` are visibility composition per [agent-scope-contexts](../../implemented/architecture/2026-07-08-agent-scope-contexts.md), not authority, and a certificate carries no durable record of which tools its session composed.
14	
15	An isolation claim above `none` therefore has no evidence behind it. `recordRun()` writes the level its caller passes; the invariant companion validates revisions, append-only check growth, and certificate coverage, and never asks what the level asserts. Keeping only `process` and `host` runs — the reward-gaming mitigation the [trajectory-export note](2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md) names, and the column the [fleet leaderboard](../../../../packages/improvement/fleet/README.md) refuses to average across — filters on an unchecked field.
16	
17	Nothing detects a workspace the implementer edited underneath its own checks. A task whose fixture supplies the tests it will be graded on is graded on whatever those files say at validation time, and the runner compares nothing between the overlay it wrote and the tree it measures.
18	
19	## Proposal
20	
21	Make the barrier authority at the executor: one policy owner, per-capability denial where each capability opens paths, and a certificate that may claim only what the composition recorded.
22	
23	**A validator-owned root.** [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier`](../../../../packages/verification/read-barrier/README.md) (`ctx.readBarrier`) at `packages/verification/read-barrier/` is the policy home for denied reads, in the role [`dsh-sandbox-policy`](../../../../packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy/README.md) plays for sandbox mode and workspace root. Its `root` config defaults to `dshHomePath('verification')` through [`dsh-home-paths`](../../../../packages/util/home-paths/README.md) and accepts any absolute or `~`-prefixed directory, as does every `denyRoots` entry; the service creates the root owner-only (`0700`) at construction and fails loud when it exists with wider modes or when a configured path is not absolute after expansion. `reserve(agent)` mints `<root>/runs/<sessionId>/` for one run and returns its absolute path, synchronously, so the role is in force the moment the caller returns; the environment runner calls it before appending the `environment/run` stamp and writes there the standard snapshot, one script per check at `checks/<checkId>`, and any fixture the environment marks held out, then resolves each check's `run` against that directory so the command line the implementer can observe in a process listing names a file whose content it cannot read. Because that reservation is what makes a session the implementer, the runner reads the barrier through `ctx.get('readBarrier')`: a composition without one reserves nothing and runs its checks inline, which is what its `isolation: none` claim already says. `protect(path)` registers one more denied directory and returns its disposer, so a plugin that owns a directory — `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` with its session-store root — contributes it as an effect instead of a deployment repeating it in configuration; `denyRoots` remains a config field for directories no plugin owns. `resolve({ session? })` answers one `ReadBarrierPolicy { role, root, denied }`, and `denies(policy, target)` decides containment. Enforcement is not a field on that policy: `enforce(capability)` registers one capability's decision as an effect and `enforcementCensus()` reads the registrations back, so what a capability enforces lives as long as its listener rather than being recomputed per call. `declareComposition(agent, { presetId, role? })` is how the preset roster — the only caller — tells the barrier what a session composed.
24	
25	| Field | Meaning |
26	|---|---|
27	| `root` (default `dshHomePath('verification')`) | Absolute or `~`-prefixed directory the barrier owns; created `0700`, rejected when it already exists with wider modes. |
28	| `denyRoots` (default `[]`) | Additional absolute directories denied alongside `root`, for directories no plugin registers through `protect()`. |
29	| `hostAttestation` (optional absolute path) | File an external account writes; without a verified one the barrier refuses a `host` claim. It arrives with the certificate invariant that reads it. |
30	
31	The denied set for a role is not among them: which authorities an `implementer` may hold is a security invariant, not a deployment choice.
32	
33	**The deny rule.** For a session whose role is `implementer`, a read is denied when the target's canonical path is a denied directory or a descendant of one. Containment is decided the way [`dsh-fs-sandbox`](../../implemented/feature/2026-07-14-cross-family-fs-sandbox.md) decides it: canonicalize first, then test identity or descent through `ctx.fs.contains(parent, child)` on resolved targets, so the policy parses no path strings and an ancestor symlink swapped since resolution is caught by re-canonicalizing immediately before the decision. A target whose containment cannot be decided is denied. Roles `validator` and `unrestricted` are denied nothing; `unrestricted` is the default and leaves every shipped preset exactly as it is today. Until a preset can declare a role, a session holding a reservation is the `implementer` and every other session is `unrestricted`, so the two open roles are indistinguishable at the decision and only the denied one is reachable.
34	
35	**The fs policy plugin.** Add `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier` at `packages/fs/fs-read-barrier/`, the read counterpart of the write and edit policy [`dsh-fs-observation-policy`](../../../../packages/fs/fs-observation-policy/README.md) contributes through the same event gate. It registers no service and declares no `Config`, because every deployment-varying value belongs to the barrier above: it injects `readBarrier` and decides one new event. [`dsh-fs`](../../../../packages/fs/fs/README.md) declares `fs/read-intent(target, actor, next)` beside `fs/write-intent` and `fs/edit-intent`, as a `@mode waterfall` returning `FsReadDenial { code: FsErrorCode; message: string } | undefined`; unlike the two single-slot intents this one delegates, because a barrier that owned the slot would stop every later read policy from deciding. The plugin returns a denial for a contained target and calls `next()` otherwise, and owns the exact message as `readBarrierDenialMessage`. `FsErrorCode` gains `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED`. `dsh-tool-fs` dispatches the event inside `resolveRegularReadTarget` before `ctx.fs.stat`, covering `read` and `read_image`, so a denied path never reveals presence or absence, and `dsh-tool-str-replace-editor` dispatches it on the `view` command. The tool layer adds no recovery instruction, because no retry of the same call succeeds; the model sees the policy's message verbatim inside the tool registry's ordinary `Error: ` framing.
36	
37	##### Exact error
38	
39	```markdown
40	read denied: "<path>" is validator-owned — it is not part of this task; continue without it
41	```
42	
43	**What a denial records.** The barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/denied` session event per refusal, carrying `{ version, role, capability, displayPath, root }`, where `capability` names the seam that refused (`fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`). The path is already in the log inside the model's own `tool/call` arguments, so the event adds evidence and no new disclosure. It is a `SessionEventMap` member registered in `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES` by `gen-persistence-catalog`, so this build reads it as a required event. The envelope's `ignorable` marker stays unused: `Session.append` has no parameter for it and no event in the repository sets it, so marking this one would be a core append change rather than a slice of the barrier.
44	
45	**Tool authority and the composition-time guard.** `ToolDefinition` in [`dsh-tools`](../../../../packages/core/tools/README.md) gains `authority?: readonly ToolAuthority[]`, never model-visible, where `ToolAuthority` is a merge-extensible union declared by `dsh-tools` with three members at the start: `session-log` (the tool reads durable session events), `plugin-mount` (it mounts or evaluates code in the live runtime), and `runtime-introspection` (it reports the live composition). `dsh-tool-session-query` declares `session-log` on all five of its tools; `dsh-tool-cordis` declares `plugin-mount` on `cordis_define`, `cordis_run`, `cordis_stop`, and `cordis_undefine`, and `runtime-introspection` on the three tools it actually ships for the read-only report — `cordis_inspect_list`, `cordis_inspect_query`, and `cordis_inspect_self`. An `implementer` session may compose none of the three. Declaring authority at the tool, rather than a name list at the barrier, means a tool added later is covered by its own declaration.
46	
47	**How a preset declares its role.** A preset's optional `preset.yml` gains `role: implementer | validator | unrestricted`, absent meaning `unrestricted`. It is the one authority claim that file carries, so [`dsh-agent-presets`](../../../../packages/preset/agent-presets/README.md) refuses `validator` from a `user`-trust preset and lists that preset as `broken` with the reason: a locally authored preset that could name itself `validator` would grant itself reads. This is the roster's first enforcing use of `trust`, and its README changes with it. `mountPreset` audits the role after `handle.await()` settles the subtree, beside `inactiveRows`, and rejects the mount when the declared role is `implementer` and any tool in the preset's scope layer declares a denied authority. Because the audit runs inside the agent factory's `setup`, a rejected composition rolls the whole session creation back, so the failure is loud and nothing half-composed survives.
48	
49	##### Exact mount refusal
50	
51	```markdown
52	agent-presets: preset "<id>" declares role "implementer" but composes "<tool>", which carries the "<authority>" authority
53	```
54	
55	**The runtime guard.** The barrier also registers one `ctx.tools.guard()` through the agent's own context at session setup, denying any execution whose definition carries a denied authority for that session's role. Guards run after every `tools/pre-execute` listener and are monotonic, so no later listener can turn the denial back into permission ([`ToolGuard`](../../../../packages/core/tools/src/index.ts)). The mount audit covers the preset's composition; the guard covers a tool registered into the agent's own layer afterwards, including one a subagent driver contributes.
56	
57	##### Exact guard denial
58	
59	```markdown
60	"<tool>" carries the "<authority>" authority and is not callable in an implementer session
61	```
62	
63	**Process-level denial.** The [sandbox seam](../../implemented/feature/2026-07-06-sandbox.md) expresses file effects only, which is why a confined subprocess can still read anything it reaches. `SandboxPolicy` and `SandboxExecutionPolicy` gain `deniedReadRoots: readonly string[]`; `ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve()` fills it from `ctx.readBarrier.resolve({ session })`, so the fs fence and every process runner keep taking one owner-resolved policy per call. `dsh-sandbox-local` implements it per backend — a `bwrap` `--tmpfs` over each root, a Landlock ruleset that omits read access for them, a Seatbelt `(deny file-read* (subpath …))` clause, and the Windows ACL runner's equivalent deny entry — and reports `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` when the selected backend cannot express the denial, so the claim fails rather than the barrier. [`dsh-bash-sandbox`](../../../../packages/shell/bash-sandbox/README.md), `dsh-pwsh-sandbox`, and [`dsh-terminal-bash`](../../../../packages/terminal/terminal-bash/README.md) inherit it without changes. [`dsh-tool-fs-search`](../../../../packages/fs/tool-fs-search/README.md) spawns ripgrep unconfined through `ctx.subprocess` today; it confines that spawn through `ctx.sandbox.confine()` whenever a barrier is in force, and additionally the barrier's tool guard denies a `glob` or `grep` whose `path` argument names a denied root directly.
64	
65	**The executor of a run.** `RunEvidence.executor` already distinguishes a `runner` from an `agent-reported` run on the `verification/run` event, and `recordRun()` certified both identically. `VerificationCertificate` gains `executor`, copied from the run it cites, so a consumer reading a certificate alone can tell which it was; the scorekeeper's outcome facts expose it as `certificateExecutor`, which is what lets a leaderboard partition on it. `recordRun()` refuses any isolation above `none` for an `agent-reported` run — the implementer's own account of its checks is admissible evidence only at the level that asserts nothing — and the invariant rejects a certificate whose executor differs from the run it cites, or which claims `process` or `host` over an `agent-reported` run.
66	
67	**Executors the barrier cannot confine.** Two composed capabilities open paths the harness cannot fence in-process. [`dsh-workflow-worker-thread`](../../../../packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/README.md) states that its worker is not a security sandbox and that an escaped script recovers Node capabilities with the host process's privileges. The out-of-process [subagent](../../../../packages/subagent/subagent/README.md) providers — `subagent-acp`, `subagent-claude-code`, `subagent-codex`, `subagent-dsh-sdk` — launch a foreign agent with its own tool stack and no harness policy. For an `implementer` session, both refuse to start under a claim of `process` or `host` and record `unenforced` under a claim of `none`. The in-process subagent drivers need no exception: a child joins its parent's standing composition through `composeFrom()`, so it inherits the same census, the same scope layer, and the same role.
68	
69	**The scope census.** It arrives with `ToolAuthority`, whose declarations its `census` is made of. Before the session's first `request/header`, the barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/scope` event carrying `{ version, role, presetId, root, denied, census, enforcement }`. `census` is one entry per tool visible to the agent, `{ name, authority }`, which makes the composition's authority durable rather than composition-time-only; the invariant cross-checks it against the tool names in each `request/header`'s assembled schemas, so a tool added after the census is caught. `enforcement` is one entry per path-opening capability the composition registered — `fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`, `subagent`, `workflow` — valued `denied-at-executor`, `unenforced`, or `not-composed`. A capability records `denied-at-executor` by calling `ctx.readBarrier.enforce(capability)` for the life of its enforcing registration, so the claim and the listener that backs it are disposed together.
70	
71	**The certificate invariant.** `recordRun()` refuses to commit a certificate whose isolation exceeds what the session recorded, with `VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN`; the [`./invariant`](../../../../packages/verification/verification/README.md) companion applies the identical rule to the durable stream, so a forged certificate fails replay wherever the companion is installed. Both read the session log alone rather than `ctx.get('readBarrier')`: everything a live barrier knows about a session is already in the census it appended, and one rule over one evidence source is what makes the live refusal and the replay refusal the same rule. Independently of level, both refuse a certificate on a session whose scope census carries a denied authority: composing a log-reading tool forfeits the certificate even when the guard was somehow bypassed. `CertificateIsolation`'s JSDoc changes with the rule: `process` means what the ladder below states rather than in-process read policy alone.
72	
73	**The `host` marker.** `host` is accepted only from a `read-barrier/attestation` event the barrier wrote after verifying a file at the configured `hostAttestation` path: it must be a regular file, be owned by a uid other than the harness process's effective uid, and be unwritable outside its owner. An in-process component cannot produce that file without already holding another account's privileges, which is the property the level asserts. The barrier records the file's SHA-256 alongside its owner; comparing that digest against the run's environment content hashes waits for the `environment/run` stamp to reach the barrier, so the shipped check proves the owner rather than the run. Ownership is read through `process.geteuid()`, which Windows does not provide: an attestation there is refused with that reason rather than verified through `dsh-sandbox-windows-acl`. Absent or unverifiable, the barrier records no attestation, logs why, and the claim is refused.
74	
75	**Tamper on check-owned paths.** Check-owned paths are the barrier's denied directories plus the workspace paths an environment declares immutable: `EnvironmentDefinition.task` gains `immutable?: readonly string[]`, workspace-relative paths the fixture supplies and the implementer must not author — the tests, the reference outputs, and any overlaid check script. The runner already hashes a directory in `hashDirectory`; it records the digest of the check-owned set immediately after the fixture overlay and before the implementer's first turn, and again at each validation. The `verification/run` event that the [environment-runner note's second slice](2026-09-05-environment-runner.md) adds carries the attempt's `treeHash`; this note adds `verdict: 'pass' | 'fail' | 'tampered'`. A digest that differs from the baseline is `tampered`: the runner records the run, issues one directive naming tamper without naming a path, stops the attempt loop because the workspace no longer measures the task, and never calls `recordRun`, so no certificate can exist for that run. `foldTrajectory` gains reward basis `tamper` with `outcome: 0`, which outranks any certificate in the same log, and the invariant companion rejects a certificate that follows a `tampered` run.
76	
77	**A blind judge under one licence.** Cross-provider routing is the first answer to a judge whose label affects it, and a deployment with one model licence cannot take it. The second route is filesystem and process isolation plus a judge session that holds no implementer context, which means all of the following and nothing weaker. The judge session is created through `ctx.agents.create` with a fresh `SessionId`, no `parentSessionId`, and no resume or fork seed, so its log begins at its own creation. Its `meta.cwd` is a judge workspace holding a copy of the implementer's tree at the audited attempt's `treeHash`, never the implementer's workspace. Its derived history contains exactly the judge preset's system prompt, the environment's task prompt, and one user message carrying the evidence the auditor chose; no `assistant/message`, `tool/result`, or `verification/directive` from the audited session reaches it. Its preset is `system`-trust and declares `role: validator`, so the composition-time guard still denies it a log-reading tool: a judge that could read the audited log would reconstruct the implementer's reasoning and lose the independence this arrangement provides. The barrier appends a `judge/session` event naming the audited session id and asserting the empty lineage, and the invariant rejects a verdict from a session whose header carries a parent or a seed.
78	
79	## The isolation ladder
80	
81	| Level | What it asserts | Required enforcement | Durable evidence |
82	|---|---|---|---|
83	| `none` | Nothing. Implementer and validator share a filesystem. | None. | The certificate alone; a scope event when the barrier is composed. |
84	| `process` | No executor of the implementer's session opens a denied path. | Every composed path-opening capability records `denied-at-executor`; the session's sandbox mode is `workspace-write` or narrower; workflow workers and out-of-process subagent providers refuse to start. | A `read-barrier/scope` event before the first `request/header`, with role `implementer`, an empty denied-authority intersection, and no `unenforced` entry. |
85	| `host` | The checks and fixtures are outside the harness account's write reach. | Everything `process` requires. | Everything `process` requires plus a `read-barrier/attestation` event the barrier verified from a file the harness process cannot write. |
86	
87	## Alternatives considered
88	
89	**Omit the tools and trust the prompt.** Schema omission and instruction are not enforcement when another caller reaches the same operation, which is why the packages standard requires the decision in the operation that makes it. The barrier denies at the executor and the acceptance criteria test denial there.
90	
91	**Deny reads through `SandboxMode` instead of a separate policy.** `SandboxMode` is a three-value file-effect vocabulary shared by every enforcing family; a fourth value meaning "and cannot read these paths" would make one enum carry two independent decisions, and every consumer that switches on the mode would have to learn the second. `deniedReadRoots` rides the same per-call policy without changing what a mode means.
92	
93	**Subclass the filesystem provider the way `fs-sandbox` does.** One provider registers `ctx.fs` per context and `SandboxedFileSystem` already extends `LocalFileSystem`, so a second fence by inheritance would force a mixin or a fixed provider ladder. The `fs/*` event gate is the layer built for adding policy without a service dependency, and it degrades to the bare provider when the plugin is absent.
94	
95	**Name the forbidden tools in the barrier's config.** A name list is stale the moment a package adds a log-reading tool, and a deployment could shorten it. Authority declared at the tool is carried by the tool, and the denied set for a role is a security invariant rather than a tunable.
96	
97	**Derive the role from the session creator instead of the preset.** The creator knows the intent; only the composition knows what was actually mounted, and the failure this prevents is a preset that composes a tool its role forbids. The preset declares the role, the mount audit checks the composition against it, and the creator's request is refused when the resolved preset's role does not match.
98	
99	**Infer `host` from configuration.** The environment runner already rejected inferred isolation for the same reason: nothing in-process can observe the deployment's arrangement, so an inferred value either devalues an isolated run or lies about a local one. A file another account owns is the smallest fact that cannot be produced from inside the process.
100	
101	**Score tamper as a failing check.** A failed check means the work is incomplete; a modified test means the measurement is void. Folding them would let a trajectory earn partial credit for a workspace whose checks no longer describe the task, so tamper is its own verdict and its own reward basis.
102	
103	**Give the judge the implementer's transcript for context.** A judge that reads the audited reasoning inherits its framing, and the same-lineage mislabeling the [seams note](2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md) records is what the blind session exists to avoid. The judge receives the task, the tree, and the evidence the auditor selected.
104	
105	## Acceptance criteria
106	
107	- In a Loader-booted composition over `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier/`, a `read` of a file under the barrier root from an `implementer`-role session fails with `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED` and the exact message above, one `read-barrier/denied` event is appended, and the same call from a session the barrier denies nothing — one holding no reservation, and a `validator` once a preset can declare that role — returns the file's content in the same process.
108	- The denial is proved through the executor, not the schema: the implementer's `read` tool is registered and visible, and a direct `ctx.fs.readText` from a trusted plugin still succeeds, which the test asserts so the threat model stays explicit.
109	- Mounting the preset at `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier-guard/`, which declares `role: implementer` and composes `dsh-tool-session-query`, rejects with the exact mount refusal and leaves no session behind; a `user`-trust preset declaring `role: validator` is listed `broken` with its reason; and the invariant companion rejects a certificate on a hand-authored log whose scope census carries the `session-log` authority.
110	- `recordRun()` with `isolation: 'host'` on a session with no verified attestation refuses with `VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN` and commits no certificate; the invariant companion rejects a hand-authored log carrying that certificate at the certificate record.
111	- `recordRun()` with `isolation: 'process'` on a session whose scope event records any `unenforced` capability refuses the same way, and succeeds once every composed capability records `denied-at-executor`.
112	- Over `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier-tamper/`, whose environment marks its test file immutable and whose scripted model overwrites it, the attempt's `verification/run` carries `verdict: 'tampered'`, no certificate exists, the goal stays out of `complete`, and the exported trajectory line has `outcome: 0` with basis `tamper`.
113	- A judge session created for an audited session has no `parentSessionId` and no seed, its derived history holds exactly the judge system prompt, the task prompt, and the evidence message, and the invariant rejects a verdict from a session that carries either.
114	- Two keyless snapshots record what the model sees: `examples/headless-agent/tests/snapshots/read-barrier-denied/` pins the denial text in the transcript and the session log, and `examples/headless-agent/tests/snapshots/read-barrier-tamper/` pins the tamper directive's `<validation_failed>` follow-up. Both replay on macOS and Linux per the [testing policy](../../../../docs/testing.md).
115	
116	## Rollout
117	
118	Each slice lands with its own tests and leaves the gates green on its own.
119	
120	1. **Landed.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier` with the root, `reserve`, `protect`, `resolve`, `denies`, `recordDenial`, the `read-barrier/denied` event, and its invariant companion, which rejects a refusal for any role but `implementer`, one carrying an unknown payload version or capability, and one naming a second barrier root inside a session. The environment runner reserves through `ctx.get('readBarrier')` and materializes `standard.json` plus one `checks/<checkId>` script per attempt, running each as `. <script>` so the same shell executes the same instruction; a check id that is not one path segment, and a reservation path the command line cannot carry unquoted, fail the run with `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT`. `read-barrier/scope` and the enforcement census are not part of it: the census is one `{ name, authority }` entry per visible tool and enforcement is one entry per capability that records a decision, so both wait for the slice that supplies their content. `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` does not yet call `protect()`, and no existing composition changes behavior.
121	2. **Landed.** `fs/read-intent` in `dsh-fs` as a delegating waterfall returning `FsReadDenial`, `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED`, the dispatches in `dsh-tool-fs` (`read` and `read_image`, inside `resolveRegularReadTarget` before the stat) and `dsh-tool-str-replace-editor` (`view`, before its own stat), and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier`, which owns the exact message. The `read-barrier` fixture proves the denial through the executor in a Loader-booted composition, and the `read-barrier-denied` snapshot pins the model-visible text and the durable record; both are keyless, the snapshot replaying a committed script through `dsh-llm-replay`.
122	3. **Landed.** `ToolAuthority` on `ToolDefinition`, the declarations in `dsh-tool-session-query` and `dsh-tool-cordis`, `role` in `preset.yml` with the `user`-trust refusal of `validator`, the `mountPreset` audit, `ReadBarrierService.declareComposition` as the roster's one way to set a role, and the per-agent tool guard. `read-barrier/scope` lands here too, with `enforce()` and `enforcementCensus()`, because the census is made of the authority declarations this slice adds and the enforcement registrations it needs a home for; `dsh-fs-read-barrier` is the first caller of `enforce()`. The audit reads the tool registry as the preset's scope resolves it, so a tool a restriction filtered out of that scope is not audited — that scope cannot call it either, and the guard covers what the audit cannot see.
123	4. **Landed.** The certificate invariant: the `recordRun` precondition, the companion's rule, `VerificationCertificate.executor` with the `agent-reported` ceiling and the scorekeeper's `certificateExecutor` fact, the `read-barrier/attestation` event and its file check, and the `CertificateIsolation` documentation change. `EnvironmentRunRequest.preset` is not part of it and is withdrawn: the census already records the session's role, so `isolationProblem` refuses a claim above `none` from a session that did not hold `implementer` — the refusal belongs to the operation that certifies, not to a second field on the run request. `verification-domain`'s `agent-reported` fixture moves from `process` to `none`, which is what its evidence supported all along.
124	5. `deniedReadRoots` on `SandboxPolicy` and `SandboxExecutionPolicy`, the `dsh-sandbox-local` backends, the `dsh-sandbox-policy` fill from the barrier, the confined ripgrep spawn in `dsh-tool-fs-search`, and the refusals in the workflow engine and the out-of-process subagent providers. This is the slice that makes `process` claimable.
125	6. Tamper: `task.immutable` in `dsh-environments`, the runner's baseline and per-attempt digest over check-owned paths, `verdict` on `verification/run`, the `tamper` reward basis in `dsh-trajectories`, and the `read-barrier-tamper` fixture and snapshot. It follows the `verification/run` event from the [environment-runner note's second slice](2026-09-05-environment-runner.md).
126	7. The blind judge: the shipped `system`-trust judge preset, the lineage-free creation path, the `judge/session` event, and the invariant that rejects a seeded judge. The judging Consumer itself belongs to the oversight seam of the [seams note](2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md).
127	
128	## Risks
129	
130	The barrier is trusted code in the implementer's own process below `host`. A plugin with direct `Session` or `ctx.fs` access appends counterfeit events and reads any path, exactly as `dsh-verification` already states for its durable records. The ladder is honest about this: `none` claims nothing, `process` claims only that the composed executors deny, and `host` is the only level whose evidence comes from outside the process.
131	
132	`process` costs enforcement a deployment may not want. Confining every ripgrep spawn, refusing workflow workers, and refusing out-of-process subagent providers removes capability from implementer sessions that claim it; a deployment that wants those capabilities runs at `none` and keeps a certificate that says so.
133	
134	A check's command line stays observable. The barrier protects the script's content and the fixtures, not the argv a process listing shows, so an environment whose check name or arguments encode the assertion leaks it. Environment authors keep the assertion in the script.
135	
136	The census is only as complete as the composition it was taken from. It is appended before the first request and cross-checked against each `request/header`'s tool names, which catches a tool added later but not a plugin that reads paths without registering a tool at all.
137	
138	Tamper detection is a digest comparison, so it reports that the check-owned set changed and never who changed it or how. A legitimate build step that rewrites a file inside the immutable set fails the run; environment authors declare the immutable set narrowly, and a false verdict costs one run rather than a wrong certificate.
139	
140	Making `trust` enforcing for one field changes what the roster promises. A deployment that configured a `user` root expecting presets to be ordinary compositions now finds one class of declaration refused there; the refusal is listed as a `broken` reason on the same roster page that offers to delete it.
141

60	  const checksSha256 = sha256(JSON.stringify(environment.checks.map(check => [check.id, check.outcome, check.run])))
61	  const contentSha256 = sha256([promptSha256, fixtureSha256 ?? '', checksSha256].join('\n'))
62	  return { promptSha256, checksSha256, ...fixtureSha256 === undefined ? {} : { fixtureSha256 }, contentSha256 }

65	function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
66	  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)
67	}

69	/** Require one non-empty string field of a durable stamp. */
70	function stampText(value: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {
71	  const field = value[key]
72	  if (typeof field !== 'string' || field === '') throw new Error(`environment/run ${key} must be a non-empty string`)
73	  return field
74	}
75	
76	/** Require one SHA-256 hex field of a durable stamp. */
77	function stampHex(value: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): string {
78	  const field = stampText(value, key)
79	  if (!HEX_64.test(field)) throw new Error(`environment/run ${key} must be a SHA-256 hex digest`)
80	  return field
81	}
82	
83	/**
84	 * Decode a value that declares itself as an environment run stamp. Unrelated
85	 * values return `undefined`; a malformed stamp fails replay loudly, as every
86	 * durable payload does at the log boundary.
87	 * @param value - candidate durable payload.
88	 * @returns the validated stamp, or `undefined` for another value kind.
89	 */
90	export function decodeEnvironmentRun(value: unknown): EnvironmentRunStamp | undefined {
91	  if (!isRecord(value) || value['kind'] !== 'environment/run') return undefined
92	  if (value['version'] !== ENVIRONMENT_RUN_VERSION) {
93	    throw new Error(`unsupported environment/run version ${String(value['version'])}`)
94	  }
95	  const heldOut = value['heldOut']
96	  if (typeof heldOut !== 'boolean') throw new Error('environment/run heldOut must be a boolean')
97	  const repetition = value['repetition']
98	  if (typeof repetition !== 'number' || !Number.isSafeInteger(repetition) || repetition < 0) {
99	    throw new Error('environment/run repetition must be a non-negative integer')
100	  }
101	  const model = value['model']
102	  if (!isRecord(model)) throw new Error('environment/run model must be a record')
103	  const isolation = value['isolation']
104	  if (typeof isolation !== 'string' || !ISOLATIONS.has(isolation)) {
105	    throw new Error('environment/run isolation must be none, process, or host')
106	  }
107	  const fixture = value['fixtureSha256'] === undefined ? {} : { fixtureSha256: stampHex(value, 'fixtureSha256') }
108	  const group = value['group'] === undefined ? {} : { group: stampText(value, 'group') }
109	  const district = value['district'] === undefined ? {} : { district: stampText(value, 'district') }
110	  return {
111	    kind: 'environment/run',
112	    version: ENVIRONMENT_RUN_VERSION,
113	    environmentId: EnvironmentId(stampText(value, 'environmentId')),
114	    environmentKind: stampText(value, 'environmentKind'),
115	    heldOut,
116	    promptSha256: stampHex(value, 'promptSha256'),
117	    checksSha256: stampHex(value, 'checksSha256'),
118	    ...fixture,
119	    contentSha256: stampHex(value, 'contentSha256'),
120	    repetition,
121	    ...group,
122	    ...district,
123	    model: { provider: stampText(model, 'provider'), model: stampText(model, 'model') },
124	    isolation: isolation as EnvironmentRunStamp['isolation'],
125	  }
126	}

136	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_DUPLICATE_ID'
137	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_NO_CHECKS'
138	  | 'ENVIRONMENT_DUPLICATE_CHECK'

140	/** Error returned by the environment registry boundary. */
141	export class EnvironmentError extends HarnessError {
142	  /**
143	   * @param message - human-readable rejection reason.
144	   * @param code - stable machine-routable classification.
145	   */
146	  // Keep the constructor to narrow HarnessError's string code at this boundary.
147	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-useless-constructor -- type-only narrowing
148	  constructor(message: string, code: EnvironmentErrorCode) {
149	    super(message, code)
150	  }
151	}

153	/**
154	 * Brand a string as an environment id.
155	 * @param id - raw environment identifier.
156	 * @returns the same string with the compile-time brand.
157	 */
158	export function EnvironmentId(id: string): EnvironmentIdType {
159	  return id as EnvironmentIdType
160	}
161	
162	/** Copy a definition so callers never share the registry's stored check list. */
163	function detach(definition: EnvironmentDefinition): EnvironmentDefinition {
164	  return { ...definition, checks: definition.checks.map(check => ({ ...check })) }
165	}
166	
167	/** Reject a definition whose verifiers cannot author a completion standard. */
168	function assertChecks(definition: EnvironmentDefinition): void {
169	  if (definition.checks.length === 0) {
170	    throw new EnvironmentError(`environment "${definition.id}" declares no checks`, 'ENVIRONMENT_NO_CHECKS')
171	  }
172	  const seen = new Set<string>()
173	  for (const check of definition.checks) {
174	    if (seen.has(check.id)) {
175	      throw new EnvironmentError(`environment "${definition.id}" declares check "${check.id}" twice`, 'ENVIRONMENT_DUPLICATE_CHECK')
176	    }
177	    seen.add(check.id)
178	  }
179	}
180	
181	/** Environment registry (`ctx.environments`): tasks with verifiers, held at composition time. */
182	export class EnvironmentRegistry extends Service {
183	  private readonly environments = new Map<EnvironmentIdType, EnvironmentDefinition>()
184	
185	  constructor(ctx: Context) {
186	    super(ctx, 'environments')
187	  }
188	
189	  /**
190	   * Register one environment. Registrations are effects: the producer keeps
191	   * the returned disposer under its own fiber so disposal removes the entry.
192	   * @param definition - complete environment definition.
193	   * @returns the exact disposer that removes this registration and no later one under the same id.
194	   * @throws {@link EnvironmentError} when the id is already registered, the
195	   *   definition declares no checks, or two checks share an id.
196	   */
197	  register(definition: EnvironmentDefinition): () => void {
198	    if (this.environments.has(definition.id)) {
199	      throw new EnvironmentError(`environment "${definition.id}" is already registered`, 'ENVIRONMENT_DUPLICATE_ID')
200	    }
201	    assertChecks(definition)
202	    const stored = detach(definition)
203	    this.environments.set(stored.id, stored)
204	    return () => {
205	      if (this.environments.get(stored.id) === stored) this.environments.delete(stored.id)
206	    }
207	  }
208	
209	  /**
210	   * Read one environment.
211	   * @param id - environment identity.
212	   * @returns a detached definition, or `undefined` when nothing is registered under the id.
213	   */
214	  get(id: EnvironmentIdType): EnvironmentDefinition | undefined {
215	    const stored = this.environments.get(id)
216	    return stored === undefined ? undefined : detach(stored)
217	  }
218	
219	  /**
220	   * List environments in registration order.
221	   * @param filter - kind and held-out selection; absent fields match everything.
222	   * @returns detached definitions.
223	   */
224	  list(filter: EnvironmentFilter = {}): EnvironmentDefinition[] {
225	    return [...this.environments.values()]
226	      .filter(environment => filter.kind === undefined || environment.kind === filter.kind)
227	      .filter(environment => filter.heldOut === undefined || environment.heldOut === filter.heldOut)
228	      .map(detach)
229	  }
230	}

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

1	/**
2	 * Environment runner: the automated validator that runs one registered
3	 * environment as one fresh session. It stamps the session with the
4	 * environment it runs, authors the completion standard from the environment's
5	 * checks, drives the implementer turn by turn, restores the fixture and
6	 * executes the checks through the shell executor after each turn, records the
7	 * run, and completes the goal only under a certificate. The
8	 * [environment-runner Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-environment-runner.md)
9	 * owns the design rationale.

114	 * shell's dialect.

116	const UNQUOTED_COMMAND_WORD = /^[A-Za-z0-9_@%+=:,./\\-]+$/

118	/** Subdirectory of a reservation holding one script per check. */
119	const CHECKS_DIR = 'checks'

130	 * a single path segment or a path the check command line cannot carry unquoted.
131	 * @param runDirectory - the reservation the barrier minted for this run.
132	 * @param checkId - the check's id, used verbatim as the script's file name.
133	 * @returns the absolute script path.

135	 */
136	function scriptPath(runDirectory: string, checkId: string): string {
137	  if (!SAFE_CHECK_SEGMENT.test(checkId)) {
138	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`check "${checkId}" cannot name a reserved script file`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT')
139	  }
140	  const script = join(runDirectory, CHECKS_DIR, checkId)
141	  if (!UNQUOTED_COMMAND_WORD.test(script)) {
142	    throw new EnvironmentRunError(`reserved check script "${script}" contains characters the check command line cannot carry unquoted`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT')
143	  }
144	  return script
145	}

147	/** Directory test that treats a missing or unreadable path as no directory. */
148	async function isDirectory(path: string): Promise<boolean> {
149	  try {
150	    return (await stat(path)).isDirectory()
151	  } catch {
152	    // stat rejects for a missing or unreadable path; both mean the caller named no usable directory.
153	    return false
154	  }
155	}

157	/** SHA-256 over every regular file under a directory: relative POSIX path, then bytes, in sorted order. */
158	async function hashDirectory(root: string): Promise<string> {
159	  const entries = await readdir(root, { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true })
160	  const files = entries.filter(entry => entry.isFile()).map(entry => join(entry.parentPath, entry.name)).sort()
161	  const hash = createHash('sha256')
162	  for (const file of files) {
163	    hash.update(relative(root, file).split(sep).join('/')).update('\0').update(await readFile(file)).update('\0')
164	  }
165	  return hash.digest('hex')
166	}

168	/**
169	 * Reject a workspace or fixture that is not an existing absolute directory,
170	 * then overlay the fixture and return its digest.
171	 * @returns the fixture digest, or `undefined` for a task without a fixture.
172	 */

174	  if (!isAbsolute(workspace) || !await isDirectory(workspace)) {

206	async function materializeChecks(runDirectory: string | undefined, standard: StandardView): Promise<Map<string, string>> {
207	  const scripts = new Map<string, string>()

219	/** Whether one executed check passed: a zero exit that neither timed out nor was aborted. */
220	function passed(result: ShellRunResult): boolean {
221	  return result.exitCode === 0 && !result.timedOut && !result.aborted
222	}

224	/** Keep the first line and the tail of longer text inside the bound. */
225	function bound(text: string, maxChars: number): string {
226	  if (text.length <= maxChars) return text
227	  const newline = text.indexOf('\n')
228	  const head = newline === -1 ? text : text.slice(0, newline)
229	  const marker = '\n…'
230	  const tailBudget = maxChars - head.length - marker.length
231	  if (tailBudget <= 0) return text.slice(0, maxChars)
232	  return `${head}${marker}${text.slice(-tailBudget)}`
233	}
234	
235	/** Render one executed check's evidence: the exit fact, then the bounded output tails. */
236	function evidenceOf(result: ShellRunResult, maxChars: number): string {
237	  const exit = result.exitCode === null ? `terminated by ${result.signal ?? 'an unknown signal'}` : `exit ${result.exitCode}`
238	  const cause = result.timedOut ? ` after the ${result.timeoutMs}ms timeout` : result.aborted ? ' after the run was aborted' : ''
239	  const lines = [`${exit}${cause}`]
240	  if (result.stdout.text !== '') lines.push(`stdout: ${result.stdout.text.trimEnd()}`)
241	  if (result.stderr.text !== '') lines.push(`stderr: ${result.stderr.text.trimEnd()}`)
242	  return bound(lines.join('\n'), maxChars)
243	}
244	
245	/** One directive per failed run: the count as root cause, the evidence as detail, never the checks themselves. */
246	function describeFailures(failures: readonly CheckResult[], maxChars: number): DirectiveRequest {
247	  return {
248	    rootCause: `${failures.length} of the standard's checks failed`,
249	    detail: bound(failures.map((failure, index) => `${index + 1}. ${failure.evidence}`).join('\n'), maxChars),
250	  }
251	}

253	/** The validator's follow-up turn after a failed run; the text is pinned by the runner README and its e2e. */
254	function followupText(directive: DirectiveRequest): string {
255	  return `<validation_failed>\n${directive.rootCause}\n${directive.detail}\nContinue working on the task; the validator runs again when you stop.\n</validation_failed>`
256	}

258	/** Sum the usage of every assistant message in a session log. */
259	function totalUsage(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): TokenUsage | undefined {
260	  const steps = events.flatMap(event => (
261	    event.type === 'assistant/message' && event.data.usage !== undefined ? [event.data.usage] : []
262	  ))
263	  if (steps.length === 0) return undefined
264	  const total: TokenUsage = {
265	    inputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.inputTokens, 0),
266	    outputTokens: steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + step.outputTokens, 0),
267	  }
268	  for (const key of ['cacheReadTokens', 'cacheWriteTokens', 'reasoningTokens'] as const) {
269	    const values = steps.flatMap((step) => {
270	      const value = step[key]
271	      return value === undefined ? [] : [value]
272	    })
273	    if (values.length > 0) total[key] = values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0)
274	  }
275	  return total
276	}

278	/** Environment runner (`ctx.environmentRuns`): one registered environment as one validated session. */
279	export class EnvironmentRunner extends Service {
280	  static inject = ['environments', 'agents', 'agentDefaultModel', 'goals', 'completionStandards', 'shell', 'sessions']
281	
282	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
283	    isolation: z.union(['none', 'process', 'host'] as const).required(),
284	    maxAttempts: z.natural().min(1).default(1),
285	    maxGoalRounds: z.natural().min(1),
286	    checkTimeoutMs: z.natural().min(1),
287	    evidenceMaxChars: z.natural().min(1).default(2000),
288	  })
289	
290	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig
291	
292	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
293	    super(ctx, 'environmentRuns')
294	    this.resolved = resolveConfig(config)
295	  }
296	
297	  /**
298	   * Run one environment as one fresh session and validate it.
299	   * @param request - environment id, absolute workspace directory, optional model route, repetition, group, district, and abort signal.
300	   * @returns the stamp, the attempts, the certificate when one run passed, and the accumulated usage.
301	   * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} for an unknown environment, an unusable
302	   *   workspace or fixture, an implementer that replaced the goal, or a lost standard.
303	   */
304	  async run(request: EnvironmentRunRequest): Promise<EnvironmentRunReport> {
305	    const definition = this.ctx.environments.get(request.environment)
306	    if (definition === undefined) {
307	      throw new EnvironmentRunError(`environment "${request.environment}" is not registered`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNKNOWN_ENVIRONMENT')
308	    }
309	    const fixtureSha256 = await prepareWorkspace(request.workspace, definition.task.fixture)
310	    const model = request.model ?? this.defaultModel()
311	    const stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp = {
312	      kind: 'environment/run',
313	      version: ENVIRONMENT_RUN_VERSION,
314	      environmentId: definition.id,
315	      environmentKind: definition.kind,
316	      heldOut: definition.heldOut,
317	      ...environmentContentHashes(definition, fixtureSha256),
318	      repetition: request.repetition ?? 0,
319	      ...request.group === undefined ? {} : { group: request.group },
320	      ...request.district === undefined ? {} : { district: request.district },
321	      model,
322	      isolation: this.resolved.isolation,
323	    }
324	    const handle = await this.ctx.agents.create({
325	      sessionId: SessionId(`environment-${randomUUID()}`),
326	      meta: { cwd: request.workspace },
327	      agentOptions: { provider: model.provider, model: model.model },
328	      ...request.signal === undefined ? {} : { signal: request.signal },
329	      setup: (agentCtx) => {
330	        installModelSelection(agentCtx, { current: { provider: model.provider, model: model.model }, assembled: undefined })
331	      },
332	    })
333	    try {
334	      return await this.drive(handle.agent, definition, stamp, request)
335	    } finally {
336	      await handle.dispose()
337	    }
338	  }
339	
340	  /** The composition's default model route, detached from the selection service. */
341	  private defaultModel(): EnvironmentRunModel {
342	    const selection = this.ctx.agentDefaultModel.currentSelection()
343	    return { provider: selection.provider, model: selection.model }
344	  }
345	
346	  /** Stamp, goal, standard, then the attempt loop; the session is flushed on every path. */
347	  private async drive(
348	    agent: Agent,
349	    definition: EnvironmentDefinition,
350	    stamp: EnvironmentRunStamp,
351	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
352	  ): Promise<EnvironmentRunReport> {
353	    const { goals, completionStandards, sessions } = this.ctx
354	    await agent.whenIdle()
355	    const runDirectory = await this.reserve(agent, definition)
356	    agent.session.append('environment/run', stamp)
357	    const goal = goals.create(agent, {
358	      objective: definition.task.prompt,
359	      ...this.resolved.maxGoalRounds === undefined ? {} : { maxGoalRounds: this.resolved.maxGoalRounds },
360	    })
361	    goals.disarm(agent)
362	    completionStandards.author(agent, { goalId: goal.id, checks: definition.checks })
363	    const attempts: EnvironmentRunAttempt[] = []
364	    let certificate: VerificationCertificate | undefined
365	    let prompt = definition.task.prompt
366	    try {
367	      for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= this.resolved.maxAttempts; attempt += 1) {
368	        agent.followup(createUserMessage({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: prompt }], source: { kind: 'user' } }))
369	        await agent.whenIdle()
370	        const standard = this.currentStandard(agent, goal.id)
371	        const treeHash = await restoreFixture(request.workspace, definition.task.fixture)
372	        const scripts = await materializeChecks(runDirectory, standard)
373	        const results = await this.execute(standard.checks, request, scripts)
374	        attempts.push({ attempt, results, treeHash })
375	        const ref = { id: standard.id, revision: standard.revision }
376	        const outcome = completionStandards.recordRun(agent, ref, this.resolved.isolation, results, {
377	          executor: 'runner',
378	          treeHash,
379	        })
380	        if (outcome.certified) {
381	          certificate = outcome.certificate
382	          const current = goals.get(agent)
383	          if (current === undefined || current.id !== goal.id) {
384	            throw new EnvironmentRunError(`the implementer replaced goal "${goal.id}"`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_GOAL_REPLACED')
385	          }
386	          goals.complete(agent, { id: current.id, revision: current.revision })
387	          break
388	        }
389	        const directive = describeFailures(outcome.failures, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars)
390	        completionStandards.issueDirective(agent, ref, directive)
391	        prompt = followupText(directive)
392	      }
393	    } finally {
394	      await sessions.flush(agent.session)
395	    }
396	    const usage = totalUsage(agent.session.events)
397	    return {
398	      environment: definition.id,
399	      sessionId: agent.id,
400	      stamp,
401	      attempts,
402	      certified: certificate !== undefined,
403	      ...certificate === undefined ? {} : { certificate },
404	      ...usage === undefined ? {} : { usage },
405	    }
406	  }

408	  /** The standard the run measures; the implementer cannot mutate it, so another goal's standard or none is an anomaly. */
409	  private currentStandard(agent: Agent, goalId: GoalId): StandardView {
410	    const standard = this.ctx.completionStandards.get(agent)
411	    if (standard === undefined || standard.goalId !== goalId) {
412	      throw new EnvironmentRunError(`the standard for goal "${goalId}" is no longer current`, 'ENVIRONMENT_RUN_STANDARD_LOST')
413	    }
414	    return standard
415	  }
416	
417	  /**
418	   * Reserve the run's validator-owned directory and stock what the checks read
419	   * from it. Without a composed barrier there is no reservation and the checks
420	   * run their instructions inline, exactly as the run's declared isolation says.
421	   * @param agent - the implementer agent this run drives.
422	   * @param definition - the environment being run, supplying the held-out fixture.
423	   * @returns the reservation, or `undefined` when no barrier is composed.
424	   */
425	  private async reserve(agent: Agent, definition: EnvironmentDefinition): Promise<string | undefined> {
426	    const barrier = this.ctx.get('readBarrier')
427	    if (barrier === undefined) return undefined
428	    const runDirectory = barrier.reserve(agent)
429	    // A held-out environment's fixture is evaluation material: the copy under
430	    // the reservation is the one an inspecting validator reads, never the
431	    // workspace overlay the implementer works in.
432	    if (definition.heldOut && definition.task.fixture !== undefined) {
433	      await cp(definition.task.fixture, join(runDirectory, FIXTURE_DIR), { recursive: true })
434	    }
435	    return runDirectory
436	  }
437	
438	  /**
439	   * Run every active check in order through the shell executor rooted at the
440	   * workspace. A reserved check runs its script; an unreserved one runs its
441	   * instruction inline.
442	   */
443	  private async execute(
444	    checks: readonly StandardCheck[],
445	    request: EnvironmentRunRequest,
446	    scripts: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
447	  ): Promise<CheckResult[]> {
448	    const results: CheckResult[] = []
449	    for (const check of checks) {
450	      const script = scripts.get(check.id)
451	      const spec = this.ctx.shell.resolve({
452	        command: script === undefined ? check.run : `. ${script}`,
453	        workdir: request.workspace,
454	        timeoutMs: this.resolved.checkTimeoutMs,
455	        signal: request.signal,
456	      })
457	      const result = await this.ctx.shell.run(spec)
458	      results.push({
459	        checkId: check.id,
460	        status: passed(result) ? 'pass' : 'fail',
461	        evidence: evidenceOf(result, this.resolved.evidenceMaxChars),
462	      })
463	    }
464	    return results
465	  }
466	}

122	/**
123	 * Light last-wins fold of the `verification` projection unit. Unlike the
124	 * strict replay fold (fold.ts: transition validation, fail-loud on malformed
125	 * changes), this transition is projection-grade: the state is plain JSON, any
126	 * non-verification or malformed event returns the same reference, and
127	 * correctness of the written change is the write side's job.
128	 * @param state - the projection covering all prior events.
129	 * @param event - the next committed session event.
130	 * @returns the next projection (same reference when the event is not a well-formed verification change).
131	 */
132	export function applyVerificationProjection(
133	  state: VerificationProjection | null,
134	  event: SessionEvent,
135	): VerificationProjection | null {
136	  try {
137	    switch (event.type) {
138	      case 'verification/standard': {
139	        const change = decodeStandardChange(event.data)
140	        if (change === undefined) return state
141	        return {
142	          standard: change.standard,
143	          directivesIssued: state?.directivesIssued ?? 0,
144	          runsRecorded: state?.runsRecorded ?? 0,
145	          createdAt: change.createdAt,
146	          updatedAt: change.updatedAt,
147	        }
148	      }
149	      case 'verification/relaxation': {
150	        const change = decodeRelaxationChange(event.data)
151	        if (change === undefined) return state
152	        return {
153	          standard: change.standard,
154	          directivesIssued: state?.directivesIssued ?? 0,
155	          runsRecorded: state?.runsRecorded ?? 0,
156	          createdAt: change.createdAt,
157	          updatedAt: change.updatedAt,
158	        }
159	      }
160	      case 'verification/run': {
161	        const change = decodeRunChange(event.data)
162	        if (change === undefined || state === null) return state
163	        return { ...state, runsRecorded: state.runsRecorded + 1 }
164	      }
165	      case 'verification/certificate': {
166	        const change = decodeCertificateChange(event.data)
167	        if (change === undefined || state === null) return state
168	        return { ...state, certificate: change.certificate }
169	      }
170	      case 'verification/directive': {
171	        const change = decodeDirectiveChange(event.data)
172	        if (change === undefined || state === null) return state
173	        return { ...state, directivesIssued: state.directivesIssued + 1 }
174	      }
175	      default:
176	        return state
177	    }
178	  } catch (_invalidPersistedVerificationChange) {
179	    return state
180	  }
181	}

266	  /**
267	   * Author the executable standard for one goal before implementation begins.
268	   * A current standard for a different goal is superseded; authoring twice
269	   * for the same goal is rejected — grow it with {@link extend} instead.
270	   * @param agent - owning live agent.
271	   * @param request - goal identity and the initial non-empty check inventory.
272	   * @returns the authored view at revision one.
273	   */
274	  author(agent: Agent, request: AuthorStandardRequest): StandardView {
275	    const checks = this.resolveChecks(request.checks, new Set())
276	    if (checks.length === 0) {
277	      throw new VerificationError('standard requires at least one check', 'VERIFICATION_INVALID_CHECK')

279	    const cache = this.prepareMutation(agent)
280	    const current = cache.state.standard
281	    if (current !== undefined && current.goalId === request.goalId) {

288	    const standard: CompletionStandardSnapshot = {
289	      id: StandardId(`standard-${randomUUID()}`),
290	      revision: 1,
291	      goalId: request.goalId,

298	  /**
299	   * Add checks to the current standard. Existing checks and relaxations are
300	   * preserved exactly; the mutation invalidates any prior certificate.
301	   * @param agent - owning live agent.
302	   * @param ref - expected current revision.

306	  extend(agent: Agent, ref: StandardRef, checks: readonly StandardCheck[]): StandardView {
307	    const cache = this.prepareMutation(agent)
308	    const current = this.expectCurrent(cache, ref)
309	    const taken = new Set<string>([
310	      ...current.checks.map(check => check.id),
311	      ...current.relaxed.map(entry => entry.check.id),
312	    ])
313	    const added = this.resolveChecks(checks, taken)
314	    if (added.length === 0) {
315	      throw new VerificationError('extend requires at least one added check', 'VERIFICATION_INVALID_CHECK')
316	    }
317	    const standard: CompletionStandardSnapshot = {
318	      ...current,
319	      revision: current.revision + 1,
320	      checks: [...current.checks, ...added],
321	    }
322	    if (standard.checks.length > this.resolved.maxChecks) {
323	      throw new VerificationError(
324	        `standard cannot exceed ${this.resolved.maxChecks} active checks`,
325	        'VERIFICATION_INVALID_CHECK',

328	    return this.commitStandard(agent, cache, 'extend', standard, this.currentCreatedAt(cache), this.nextMutationTime(cache))

352	      ...current,
353	      revision: current.revision + 1,
354	      checks: current.checks.filter(check => check.id !== checkId),

359	      version: VERIFICATION_CHANGE_VERSION,

363	      updatedAt: this.nextMutationTime(cache),
364	    }

369	  /**
370	   * Record one complete run of the current standard. Every run appends a
371	   * durable `verification/run` event carrying all of its results; a fully
372	   * passing run then commits a certificate, while any failure returns the
373	   * failing subset the validator aggregates into a {@link issueDirective}
374	   * directive.
375	   * @param agent - owning live agent.
376	   * @param ref - expected current revision.
377	   * @param isolation - isolation level the run executed under.
378	   * @param results - exactly one result per active check, any order.
379	   * @param evidence - executor of the checks and the workspace digest it covered.
380	   * @returns the certificate, or the failing results.
381	   * @throws {@link VerificationError} with `VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN`
382	   *   when the session's durable record does not support the claimed isolation.
383	   */
384	  recordRun(
385	    agent: Agent,
386	    ref: StandardRef,
387	    isolation: CertificateIsolation,
388	    results: readonly CheckResult[],
389	    evidence: RunEvidence,
390	  ): RunOutcome {
391	    const cache = this.prepareMutation(agent)
392	    const current = this.expectCurrent(cache, ref)
393	    // Before anything is committed: the run event carries the claim too, so an
394	    // unproven level must not reach the log at all.
395	    const unproven = isolationProblem(agent.session.events, isolation, evidence.executor)
396	    if (unproven !== undefined) {
397	      throw new VerificationError(
398	        `run cannot claim "${isolation}" isolation: ${unproven}`,
399	        'VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN',
400	      )
401	    }
402	    const byCheck = new Map<string, CheckResult>()
403	    for (const result of results) {
404	      if (byCheck.has(result.checkId)) {
405	        throw new VerificationError(`duplicate result for check "${result.checkId}"`, 'VERIFICATION_INVALID_RESULTS')
406	      }
407	      byCheck.set(result.checkId, {
408	        checkId: result.checkId,
409	        status: result.status,
410	        evidence: this.text(result.evidence, `result for "${result.checkId}"`, 'VERIFICATION_INVALID_RESULTS'),
411	      })
412	    }
413	    const ordered: CheckResult[] = []
414	    for (const check of current.checks) {
415	      const result = byCheck.get(check.id)
416	      if (result === undefined) {
417	        throw new VerificationError(`run is missing a result for check "${check.id}"`, 'VERIFICATION_INVALID_RESULTS')
418	      }
419	      byCheck.delete(check.id)
420	      ordered.push(result)
421	    }
422	    const extra = [...byCheck.keys()]
423	    if (extra.length > 0) {
424	      throw new VerificationError(
425	        `run answers unknown check(s) ${extra.map(id => `"${id}"`).join(', ')}`,
426	        'VERIFICATION_INVALID_RESULTS',
427	      )
428	    }
429	    const standard: StandardRef = { id: current.id, revision: current.revision }
430	    const run: VerificationRunChangeMeta = {
431	      kind: 'verification/run',
432	      version: VERIFICATION_CHANGE_VERSION,
433	      standard,
434	      attempt: nextRunAttempt(cache.state, current.id),
435	      isolation,
436	      executor: evidence.executor,
437	      results: ordered,
438	      ...evidence.treeHash === undefined ? {} : { treeHash: evidence.treeHash },
439	      recordedAt: this.nextMutationTime(cache),
440	    }
441	    this.commit(agent, cache, 'verification/run', run)
442	    const failures = ordered.filter(result => result.status === 'fail')
443	    if (failures.length > 0) return { certified: false, failures }
444	    const certificate: VerificationCertificate = {
445	      standard,
446	      goalId: current.goalId,
447	      isolation,
448	      executor: evidence.executor,
449	      results: ordered,
450	      recordedAt: this.nextMutationTime(cache),
451	    }
452	    const change: CertificateChangeMeta = {
453	      kind: 'verification/certificate',
454	      version: VERIFICATION_CHANGE_VERSION,
455	      certificate,
456	    }
457	    this.commit(agent, cache, 'verification/certificate', change)
458	    return { certified: true, certificate }
459	  }

541	  /** Validate, trim, and cap one recorded text. */
542	  private text(value: string, field: string, code: VerificationErrorCode): string {
543	    const trimmed = value.trim()
544	    if (trimmed.length === 0) {
545	      throw new VerificationError(`${field} must be a non-empty string`, code)
546	    }
547	    if (trimmed.length > this.resolved.maxTextChars) {
548	      throw new VerificationError(`${field} exceeds ${this.resolved.maxTextChars} characters`, code)
549	    }
550	    return trimmed
551	  }

553	  /** Validate one added check inventory against ids already taken. */
554	  private resolveChecks(checks: readonly StandardCheck[], taken: Set<string>): StandardCheck[] {
555	    if (checks.length > this.resolved.maxChecks) {
556	      throw new VerificationError(
557	        `standard cannot exceed ${this.resolved.maxChecks} active checks`,
558	        'VERIFICATION_INVALID_CHECK',
559	      )
560	    }
561	    const resolved: StandardCheck[] = []
562	    const seen = new Set<string>(taken)
563	    for (const check of checks) {
564	      if (!isKebabCase(check.id)) {
565	        throw new VerificationError(`check id "${check.id}" must be lower-kebab-case`, 'VERIFICATION_INVALID_CHECK')
566	      }
567	      if (seen.has(check.id)) {
568	        throw new VerificationError(`check id "${check.id}" is already taken`, 'VERIFICATION_INVALID_CHECK')
569	      }
570	      seen.add(check.id)
571	      resolved.push({
572	        id: check.id,
573	        outcome: this.text(check.outcome, `check "${check.id}" outcome`, 'VERIFICATION_INVALID_CHECK'),
574	        run: this.text(check.run, `check "${check.id}" run`, 'VERIFICATION_INVALID_CHECK'),
575	      })
576	    }
577	    return resolved
578	  }

582	    this.assertLive(agent)
583	    const cache = this.cache(agent.session)
584	    this.sync(agent.session, cache)
585	    return cache

588	  /** Reject stale or missing current-state refs. */
589	  private expectCurrent(cache: VerificationCache, ref: StandardRef): CompletionStandardSnapshot {
590	    const current = cache.state.standard
591	    if (current === undefined) {
592	      throw new VerificationError('no current completion standard', 'VERIFICATION_STANDARD_NOT_FOUND')
593	    }
594	    if (ref.id !== current.id || ref.revision !== current.revision) {
595	      throw new VerificationError(
596	        `stale standard ref "${ref.id}" revision ${ref.revision}; current is "${current.id}" revision ${current.revision}`,
597	        'VERIFICATION_STALE_REVISION',
